ARDUINO MEGA 2560 PLUG-AND-PLAY SHIELD (REV 7.0)

Zero-Soldering Modular Connection PCB for PecoDropDesktopApp/Arduino/RVM_Arduino/RVM_Arduino.ino

Rev 7.0 Verified
Why Use This Shield Instead of Hand Soldering?
The PecoDrop RVM firmware utilizes 8 ultrasonic distance sensors (32 wires), 6 high-torque servos (18 wires), 1 inductive metal sensor (3 wires), 1 HX711 24-bit load cell (4 wires), and dual power buses. Hand-soldering over 55 loose wires creates a fragile rat's nest susceptible to vibration disconnects, sensor crosstalk, and servo brown-out resets.
The Solution: This custom shield plugs directly on top of the Arduino Mega 2560. All sensors and servos plug into labeled 3-pin and 4-pin headers. Zero loose jumper wires • Zero soldering during machine assembly • 100% plug-and-play maintenance.

Figure 1: Custom Arduino Mega 2560 Expansion Shield REV 7.0 Plug-and-Play Hardware Map

Dual Isolated Power Architecture
  • 12V DC Main Input: Powers industrial NPN proximity sensor and on-board buck step-downs via 5.08mm screw terminal.
  • 6V 5A High-Torque Servo Rail: Dedicated copper traces rated for 5A continuous draw to prevent Arduino Mega brown-outs.
  • 5V Logic Rail: Clean, low-noise supply for all 8 HC-SR04 sensors and HX711 24-bit strain gauge ADC.
Ordering from JLCPCB / PCBWay (2-Minute Process)
  • Step 1: Download RVM_Arduino_Mega_PlugAndPlay_Shield_Gerbers.zip.
  • Step 2: Visit JLCPCB.com or PCBWay.com and click Add Gerber.
  • Step 3: Select 2 Layers, Dimensions 101.6 × 53.3 mm, 1.6mm FR-4, 1oz Copper.
  • Cost: Approx $2.00 to $4.00 for 5 boards with professional silkscreen and pre-drilled holes.

Home Fabrication via Toner Transfer / CNC
If fabricating locally instead of ordering from JLCPCB:
  • Open RVM_Arduino_Mega_Shield_1to1_Drill_and_Etch_Film.pdf.
  • Print Page 2 (Mirrored Mask) on a laser printer at 100% scale onto glossy transfer paper.
  • Verify the 100.00 mm calibration ruler with digital calipers.
  • Iron onto 1.6mm single/double-sided FR-4 copper board at 200°C for 3 minutes, then etch in Ferric Chloride.
Initial Power-Up Checklist
  • Step 1: Before plugging the shield onto the Arduino Mega, connect 12V and verify 5.0V on logic pins and 6.0V on servo headers using a multimeter.
  • Step 2: Plug shield onto the Arduino Mega 2560 gently, ensuring all pin headers seat without bending.
  • Step 3: Plug in each sensor cable one by one. Run CMD:TEST_SERVOS and CMD:TEST_SENSORS over Serial Monitor at 115200 baud.
